title: A seven-feature model estimates complications after congenital heart reoperation
summary: Researchers trained a retrospective seven-feature risk model in 1,011 adults undergoing repeat congenital heart surgery. The selected gradient-boosted model reported test AUC 0.763 and validation AUC 0.782 for a composite of death and major complications. External validation and evidence of clinical benefit remain absent.
ai_technology: XGBoost gradient boosting and SHAP feature analysis

source_review.scope: Original full-text bibliographic date, relevant computational/statistical Methods and Results, bounded cohort and selection caveats; no operational clinical instructions.

evidence.tested: The 2010–2022 single-center cohort was randomly split 70%/20%/10% for training/testing/validation. Eighteen preselected clinical variables were reduced to seven using SHAP contribution. Systemic ventricular ejection fraction was most influential in the fitted models. Reduced-model test/validation AUCs were .763/.782, with reported validation CI .568–.804 and five-fold range .631–.764.
evidence.unknown: Authors selected a model at the 90th percentile AUC from bootstrapped model distributions; this is not an unbiased locked-model estimate. Rare composite events, single-center surgical selection and feature/model selection constrain generalization. Logistic-regression AUC .727 had overlapping confidence intervals, so superiority is not established. Conventional survival analysis of heart failure is separate from the machine-learning result, and SHAP influence is not causation.
evidence.ai_role: Gradient boosting fitted clinical variables to a composite postoperative outcome; SHAP ranked model contributions and supported a reduced seven-variable model.
